reading: The UK government and the EU plan to release two treaties, or formal agreements between governments, on Thursday afternoon.
The treaties cover food trade and emissions trading, a system for buying and selling permission to release gases that warm the planet.
The BBC understands that the treaties contain a clause, or rule, about ending the deal within ten years.
If either side ended the deal during that period, it would have to pay to rebuild border facilities.
These border facilities would be significantly scaled back as part of the deal.
Food exporters are expected to benefit from fewer border checks and less red tape, meaning difficult official procedures.
An internal analysis forecasts a 16% increase in agricultural exports as a result of the changes.
The government and industry hope that savings for food businesses will be passed on to customers.
However, shoppers might not notice a clear difference in prices at the checkout.
The deal has already sparked debate about its benefits, costs and the future relationship between the UK and the EU.
Opposition leader Kemi Badenoch and Reform UK's Nigel Farage have suggested they would refuse to pay the costs of ending the deal.
